entries.note: Clegg 2012 (PMID 22266222, epub 2012-01-20) resolves; quote verbatim in abstract. Quote is about efficacy, not the reporter readout; luciferase readout confirmed in FDA review NDA 210951 (LNCaP/AR-Luc, 10 mg/kg/d). Untested opener fine.

Rathkopf 2013 (PMID 24002508, epub 2013-09-03) quote verbatim; FDHT-PET fell at all doses (direct). Reporter vs PSA as proximal AR transcriptional output is reasonable. Registry date 2018-07-27 confirmed for NCT01171898.

Clegg abstract states 30 mg/kg/d maximal response and 'higher therapeutic index with a greater potential to reach maximally efficacious doses in man'. AUC ~160.3 µg·h/mL projection confirmed in FDA review (lines ~1293-1297). margin_stated is qualitative only.

Status same holds (reached, worked, no MTD to 480 mg). Fix fields: Rathkopf does not set the model projection beside patient PK, so comparison_stated false, source_calls_it null. Margin weak: dog convulsions at Cmax 7 µg/mL vs human 6 µg/mL.
Clegg 2012 abstract quote verbatim; 8/10 tumours regressed >50% at 10 mg/kg confirmed in FDA review.

Smith 2016 (PMID 27160947, epub 2016-05-06): primary endpoint 12-wk PSA response, quote verbatim; nmCRPC on ADT matches castrate model. NCT registry dates for all four patient_trials confirmed. Judgement's proxalutamide reason is wrong (see missing).

FDA review quote verbatim (line 1093); dog convulsions 25 mg/kg/d, GABA-A IC50 3.0/0.88 µM; label seizure 0.2%; ARAMIS 0.2% both arms confirmed. Latest status same stands, but cell must open with an untested entry at model_first_use_year 2010 (proxy).

missing: Proxalutamide (pruxelutamide, a class member) has an in-vivo model: Zhou 2020 Eur J Cancer, doi:10.1016/j.ejca.2020.04.013 (PMID 32460179), 'The efficacy of GT0918 was investigated in a castration-resistant xenograft model' plus phase 1 (PSA>=50% in 2/16). The draft's claim that its preclinical work is cell lines only is wrong. Kintor announced (Sept 2020 IDMC; tier 5, e.g. Kintor 2020 interim results, en.kintor.com.cn/news/131.html) that the 2L+ mCRPC phase 3 missed interim rPFS. It needs its own model_id entry in efficacy: probably untested (model never tested post-abiraterone/docetaxel disease), otherwise contra. The trial population was not verified.

Darolutamide's own model (castration-resistant VCaP xenograft; FDA review NDA 212099, lines ~1364-1378) is only mentioned in a judgement. As a different system, it should get its own model_id entries (efficacy vs ARADES NCT01317641 / ARAMIS; safety, where mouse brain:plasma was low and ARAMIS seizures were 0.2% in both arms).

Rezvilutamide (SHR3680): CHART phase 3 in high-volume mHSPC was positive, but no published in-vivo model was found, so no entry is needed. TRC-253 (JNJ-63576253): preclinical xenografts in Branch 2021 MCT (doi:10.1158/1535-7163.MCT-20-0510); the phase 1/2a primary endpoint was DLT, so it is unscored, as the draft says.
rule_questions: Safety: when the filed animal toxicity (dog convulsions at a Cmax at or near the human Cmax) predicts a harm at clinical exposure and patients show it at 0.2%, is that 'same' in direction, or does the magnitude need to be recorded as over_predicted?

Rule 6 opener: when the model's first use (2010 dog study) became public only in the same document that carries the comparison (2018 FDA review), is an untested opener at model_first_use_year still required? The draft skipped it and lint did not flag it.

Population mismatch for a member drug on its own model: if a castration-resistant (NHA-naive) xenograft is paired with a post-abiraterone phase 3 failure (proxalutamide), is the cell untested under 'conditions the model never tested', or contra?
